page: Amazon Web Services m8gb.2xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an ARM64 architecture utilizing an 8-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor running at 2.8 GHz. The CPU allocation is fully dedicated, with one thread per physical core and no hyperthreading. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or a dedicated GPU, but features a baseline network bandwidth of 17 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the m8gb.2xlarge demonstrates solid mid-range capabilities. Its PassMark memory score is highly competitive, placing in the top tier (top 10%). The single-threaded bzip3 decompression performance is also strong, ranking in the top 25% with a rate of 14.46 GB/sec. Most other compute and memory benchmarks, including stress-ng, Geekbench, and Redis SET operations, register in the average middle 50% range. However, the instance shows limitations in cryptographic operations, with its PassMark CPU encryption test scoring in the bottom 25%. Additionally, LLM inference for medium 7B models results in a poor prompt processing speed of 15.66 tokens/sec, though text generation remains average at 11.96 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m8gb.2xlarge offers a balanced resource density for general-purpose workloads that benefit from dedicated ARM64 cores and high memory bandwidth without the premium of x86 licensing. Tradeoffs include the complete lack of local NVMe storage and the absence of advanced x86 instruction sets like AVX or AMX. This configuration is appropriate for application servers, static web serving, Redis caching, and lightweight containerized microservices.
